title: Midweek candidate insights - Avery Ly
content:
Quick brain dump after the loop with Avery Ly (senior inference engineer candidate). This is a raw scratchpad — focus on patterns, follow-ups, and an initial calibration vs our role rubric. Share with Priya/Marcus for quick sync before updating the scorecard.

Context and background
- Came from a mid-size ML infra company (EdgeScale) where they owned model-serving infra for multi-tenant quantized LLMs. Spent ~3.5 years there.
- Strong ownership story: led rollout of a new KV cache tier and implemented a cross-tenant cold-start mitigation that reduced p99 latency by ~18% for short-sequence traffic.
- Recent side-project: prototype for memory-efficient KV serialization for 4-bit quantized checkpoints (not yet OSS).

High-level impression (gut)
- Solid practical engineer: knows trade-offs between latency and batching, and pragmatic about engineering debt. Comfortable with ops/infra + some systems design.
- Communication: clear, focused, but tendency to default to implementation detail early. Needs nudges to zoom out to product/SLAs.
- Culture fit: collaborative, asked good clarifying Qs about our rollout cadence and monitoring. Appears to prefer small cross-functional teams vs large orgs.

Technical assessment (notes)
- Architecture/design exercise (30m): Asked to design a fallback routing policy and cache invalidation strategy for model variant degradations.
  - Strengths: Proposed a multi-tier fallback (same-arch quantized variant -> smaller context model -> remote hosted endpoint) and concrete circuit-breaker thresholds tied to p50/p95 token cost.
  - Misses: Initially omitted impact on KV cache coherency across variants (I prompted, then they added a write-through shim idea).
  - Implementation detail: Suggested using epoched cache keys with model-version namespace; good practical approach but didn't surface race conditions with rolling updates until probed.

- Systems debug (whiteboard kernel perf): Had a crisp explanation for head-of-line blocking with small-batch sequential calls and proposed two mitigation axes: continuous micro-batching and adaptive batching windows based on per-route latency SLO. Gave plausible pseudo-code for batching loop.

- Trial project (takehome summary) — did the mini-proj we gave (simple KV cache + eviction test harness).
  - Outcome: Clean code, good test coverage, used a small benchmark harness with synthetic sequences. Observed results reported: 12–20% reduction in per-token compute in synthetic runs (depends on cache hit rate).
  - Things to probe: Harness didn’t simulate multi-model cache or concurrent rollouts; artifact note says "left TODO: multi-tenant isolation tests."

Behavioral / leadership
- Ownership: Examples of shipping infra features end-to-end, including stakeholder alignment and post-mortem. Uses data for decisions (e.g., rolling back when p99 > target).
- Mentorship: Mentions mentoring two junior SWE hires; concrete examples of code reviews and pairing.
- Tradeoff judgement: Picks pragmatic short-term fixes when service pressure is high, but also advocates for longer-term infra investments when there’s clear ROI.

Red flags / areas to verify
- Depth on low-level kernels (CUDA/ROCm): Comfortable at the inference-system pattern level but lighter on custom kernel design. For roles that require custom operator work, this is borderline.
- Testing at scale: Tests looked well-structured but the takehome didn’t address chaos/injection testing at scale; ask for past examples if we move forward.
- Cross-team shipping: Prefers small, fast-moving teams — need to verify experience navigating enterprise compliance/sigapproval (if we think they'd join Dedicated/Private projects).

Quick scorecard (initial, on our internal 1-5 scale)
- System design (serving/runtime): 4/5 (strong pragmatic design, missed a couple race conditions initially)
- Implementation (code quality, tests): 4/5 (clean, test-first; left some multi-tenant TODOs)
- Deep ops/kernel expertise: 3/5 (great system-level knowledge, lighter on custom kernel internals)
- Communication & collaboration: 4/5 (clear, slightly detail-biased)
- Leadership / ownership: 4/5 (good examples, hands-on)
- Overall fit for senior inference engineer (team A): 4/5 (would recommend as a hire for runtime/platform teams that pair ops+systems work)

Suggested follow-ups / interview plan if we progress
- Ask for one short artifact: a short write-up (1–2 pages) describing a past rollout that went wrong and the post-mortem; specifically ask for metrics chosen, detection time, rollback vs fix decision, and stakeholder comms. This will surface scale testing and cross-org handling.
- Optional deep-dive: Pairing session focused on kernel/quantization tradeoffs if we need stronger low-level coverage.
- Reference checks: Prior manager at EdgeScale (contact on resume) focused on shipping large infra changes and collaboration with product/security.

Notes for calibration vs rubric
- Score leans toward hire-for-impact quickly: Avery reduces ops friction and has solid short-term wins. Not the top pick if we need someone to write custom CUDA kernels tomorrow.
- Compared to recent finalists: sits between Samira (stronger kernel depth) and Ramon (stronger shipping/ops). If candidates above are unavailable, Avery is a strong option.

Action items (my immediate next steps)
- Send brief note to Priya & Marcus with this pad and propose doing the artifact ask as a next step.
- Add a short bullet list question pack for the post-mortem artifact (I’ll draft).
- If Priya/Marcus agree, request availability for a 60m pairing session (kernel/quantization) next week.

Random micro-notes (tangents worth saving)
- Liked the "epoched cache keys" phrasing — could be worth pulling into our internal design lexicon if we adopt similar approach.
- Candidate emphasized measuring "token-cost-per-request" as a primary dial — aligns with our Optimize messaging.

End scratchpad — will convert to a concise scorecard + next-steps email once Priya/Marcus give thumbs up.
